uni.intro: Academic partners connect to the competency framework and the talent pipeline. Every partner listed here has a public source.

ku.title: Nuclear engineering degrees
ku.body: MSc in Nuclear Engineering since 2010, aimed at careers at FANR, ENEC and ENEC Operations; a PhD in Engineering with a nuclear concentration since 2012; and a BSc nuclear minor.
ku.source: Khalifa University · MSc in Nuclear Engineering

entc.title: Emirates Nuclear Technology Center
entc.body: Launched in November 2019 with ENEC and FANR. Works on nuclear safety, materials and chemistry, and radiation safety.

ep.title: Energy Pioneers
ep.body: Since 2009, "over 500 UAE Nationals benefitted". Partner universities in the UAE, the United States (Penn State, Texas A&M, NC State) and Korea.

nitss.title: Nuclear Innovation & Technology Summer School
nitss.body: The 2024 summer school had 60 participants from 20 universities.
nitss.source: UAE National Report, 10th CNS Review Meeting

iat.title: Technical school routes
iat.body: The Institute of Applied Technology feeds the technician pipeline. Abu Dhabi Polytechnic ran the former Higher Diploma in Nuclear Technology, which the Diploma in Nuclear Technology replaced in 2023.
iat.source: UAE National Report, 10th CNS Review Meeting

src.title: Saskatchewan Research Council and GIEMS
src.body: A January 2026 memorandum of understanding on small modular reactors, AI and robotics, waste and capacity building. MoUs are non-binding evaluations.

uni.partnersHint: Filter by type or country. Relationships are listed only where a public source exists.
uni.digestNote: Entries marked "search digest only" come from secondary summaries and are kept until a primary source is found.
uni.internshipsHint: Placements ENEC publishes for university students. Applications are made through the internships programme.
uni.internshipsApply: How to apply for an internship
uni.alignHint: Choose the roles your graduates target to see and export the competencies and levels they need.
uni.joinRule1: The university workspace shows only students who have consented to share their progress with that university.
uni.joinRule2: Sponsors see individual scholar progress; universities see consenting students and cohort totals only.
uni.joinRule3: Research proposals are screened for security sensitivity and export control before any public mention.
uni.consentBody: Students decide whether their university can see their progress, and can withdraw that consent at any time.

curr.title: Competencies for target roles
curr.intro: Pick one or more roles. The table lists every competency those roles need, the highest required proficiency level and whether it is core.
curr.note: Security, safeguards and cyber roles are not listed here: they show the career path only.

ip.moet: Refer inventions to the MoET patents route (May 2026)
ip.source: ENEC and the Ministry of Economy and Tourism: IP agreement (May 2026)

res.intro: Curated public problem statements. Researchers respond with a proposal; inventions are referred to the patents route agreed with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism in May 2026.
res.screenBody: A challenge is published only after a screening sign-off for security sensitivity and export control, recorded in the audit log. Research data about the plant never goes on public pages.
res.partnersOnly: Proposals come from partner organisations and universities.
res.signInPartner: Sign in as a partner to propose
res.rule1: Do not include plant data, security-sensitive information or export-controlled content in a proposal.
res.rule2: Each proposal is screened before it is accepted or mentioned publicly.
res.rule3: Partners see only their own organisation's proposals.
res.ipBody: Where a proposal may lead to an invention, it is referred to the patents route that ENEC agreed with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.

pu.intro: Your university's internship placements, consenting scholars, cohort totals and curriculum alignment.
pu.consentBody: A student appears here only if they consented to share their progress with your university. Students who have not consented are not shown, not counted and not hinted at.
pu.noOrg: Your organisation could not be loaded.
pu.noOnboarding: No onboarding case is recorded for your organisation.
pu.onboardingNote: Onboarding is handled by ENEC's partnerships team; the status here is read-only.
pu.noCohorts: No cohorts are recorded at your university.
pu.noScholarsBody: No student has consented to share their progress with your university yet.
pu.scholarsNote: Scholars are identified by reference only. Progress notes and grades stay with the sponsor.
pu.internshipsHint: Placements reserved for your university and placements open to any university.
pu.internshipsNote: Students apply through the internships programme; ENEC HR screens every application.

pr.intro: Respond to a published challenge or propose open research. Proposals are screened for security sensitivity and export control before any decision or public mention.
pr.safeBody: Do not include plant data, security arrangements, export-controlled technical data or personal data. Screening will decline any proposal that does.
pr.mineHint: Only your organisation can see these. Drafts can be edited; submitted proposals are locked.
pr.title: Title
pr.ipHint: Choose the patents route if the work may lead to an invention.
pr.challengesHint: Each challenge has passed a screening sign-off.
pr.stepsNote: ENEC's research screening authority checks security sensitivity and export control, routes IP, then accepts or declines.
pr.confirmBody: The proposal is locked and sent for security and export-control screening. ENEC records the decision; you will see it here.

ar.intro: Curate research challenges, sign off screening and decide proposals. Every action is recorded in the audit log.
ar.ruleBody: A challenge is public only when both the security-sensitivity and export-control checks are signed. Editing a published challenge takes it off the public page until it is screened again.
ar.readOnly: Read-only view: only the research screening authority acts here.
ar.themeHint: For example: Learning, Environment, Health & safety.
ar.editWarning: Saving changes takes this challenge off the public page until a new screening sign-off.
ar.securityHint: No plant security arrangements, plant data or clearance-related content.
ar.exportHint: No controlled technology or technical data.
ar.willPublish: Both checks signed: the challenge will be published.
ar.wontPublish: Not both checks signed: the result is recorded and the challenge stays unpublished.

decideBody.screening: "{title}" moves to screening. The partner sees the new status.
decideBody.accepted: "{title}" is accepted. Acceptance needs a completed security and export-control screening.
decideBody.declined: "{title}" is declined. The partner sees the decision.

ar.proposalScreen: Screened: no security-sensitive or export-controlled content
ar.proposalScreenHint: Required before a proposal can be accepted.
ar.auditHint: Every research action, including refusals, from the append-only audit log.

links.uaBody: Universities map their programmes to ENEC skills and levels. Endorsed programmes give graduates validated evidence at hire.
links.uaPublic: Partner universities sign in to map their programmes.
links.fwBody: Fellows work inside real ENEC research challenges or ADVANCE studies; sponsored study comes with a placement. Completion rate is the headline.
links.signIn: Sign in to see fellowships and completion rates.

reasons.ua_role: {role} ({horizon}): {covered} of {n} requirements reach their teachable target, score {score}
reasons.ua_rule: FS57 rule: credit up to level 2, core requirements weigh double; endorsement needs a best score of {min}

ua.sampleBody: Programme rows in this demo are illustrative mappings for the platform, not actual ENEC endorsements of any university's degree.
ua.notAuthority: Kafa'a records alignment for recognition at hire; it does not accredit degrees or issue qualifications.
ua.nqfNote: NQF levels are indicative and stated by the university; Kafa'a does not place qualifications on the framework.

cov.noRoles: Choose target roles to see coverage.
cov.rule: Same rule as the curriculum coverage scorer (FS57): the programme is the teaching source; levels 3 and 4 are built on the job.

crit.outcomes: Every mapped skill names the modules that teach it
crit.coverage: At least one target role reaches coverage {min}
crit.crosswalk: Every mapped skill has a published international anchor (crosswalk)
crit.assessment: The programme assesses each mapped skill
crit.placement: The programme includes an industry placement or project
crit.accreditation: The programme holds its national accreditation (reference on file)

problem.code: Give a programme code of 2 to 30 letters, digits, spaces, dots, dashes or slashes.
problem.title: Give the title in English and Arabic (3 to 160 characters each).
problem.nqf: The indicative NQF level is a whole number from 1 to 10, or empty.
problem.field: The field of study is at most 120 characters in each language.
problem.summary: The summary is at most 600 characters in each language.
problem.roles: Choose 1 to 4 current ENEC roles (security roles are career-path only).
problem.skills: Map 3 to 30 different skills, each at level 1 or 2 with 1 to 6 modules (2 to 80 characters).
problem.accreditation: The accreditation reference is at most 120 characters.

ws.intro: Map each programme to ENEC skills and levels, naming the modules that teach each skill. Coverage and the computed endorsement criteria update as you edit; submit when ready for review.
ws.noneBody: Add a programme to see how it covers ENEC role profiles.
ws.note: You see only your own university's programmes. Revising an endorsed programme starts a new version that needs a new review; evidence already written stays.

ed.nqfHint: 1 to 10, as stated by the university
ed.placement: Includes an industry placement or project
ed.ceiling: Programmes map skills up to level {max}: higher levels are built on the job.
ed.submitConsequence: A framework owner at ENEC reviews the programme. You cannot edit it while it is under review.

reg.intro: Every university programme mapped to ENEC skills, with coverage from the FS57 rule and the computed endorsement criteria. Framework owners endorse or return submitted programmes; the person who submitted never decides.
reg.addBehalf: Add on behalf of a university
reg.queueLine: Best role coverage {best} with {n} mapped skills.

detail.intro: Coverage of the target roles, the mapped skills with their modules and international anchors, the endorsement and its history.
detail.notFoundBody: It does not exist or it belongs to another university.
detail.skillsBody: Each skill names the modules that teach it; anchors come from the international crosswalk.
detail.waiting: Waiting for a framework owner's review.
detail.ownSubmission: You submitted this programme, so another framework owner must decide it.
detail.coversHint: Within the three years before today; the endorsement then runs for three years.
detail.noteHint: 10 to 500 characters; the university sees it.
detail.endorseConsequence: The programme is endorsed for three years. Graduates already recorded at hire whose graduation date it covers receive validated evidence for the mapped skills now. This is written to the evidence ledger.
detail.returnConsequence: The university sees your note and can edit and resubmit. No evidence is written.

gh.intro: Record a graduate at hire. Kafa'a writes validated evidence for the programme's mapped skills only when the programme is endorsed and its window covers the graduation date.
gh.ruleBody: A graduate of a programme that is not endorsed waits; the evidence is written when the programme is endorsed, if the graduation date is covered. Evidence is capped at level 2 and observed on the graduation date.
gh.recordConsequence: The hire is recorded. If the programme is endorsed and covers the graduation date, validated evidence is written for every mapped skill and the person's skills are recomputed.

fw.intro: Fellows learn inside real ENEC projects: NEST-style fellowships in a research challenge or an ADVANCE technology study, and sponsored study paired with a placement. We report the completion rate, computed from milestones, before any award count.
fw.nestBody: A graduate student or early-career professional works inside a real project with a named supervisor role card: research plan, midpoint review, deliverable, final report and knowledge transfer.
fw.mscfpBody: Study funding paired with a placement at ENEC: the university reports enrolment, year results and graduation; ENEC signs off the placement.
fw.headline: Completion rate
fw.headlineBody: Completed fellowships divided by those due (complete, withdrawn or past their planned end). Groups with fewer than {n} due are suppressed.
fw.noStatsTitle: Aggregates are for staff, partners and HR
fw.noStatsBody: Your own fellowships are listed below.
fw.definition: A fellowship is complete when every required milestone is signed off by its supervisor or HR, never by the person who submitted it.
fw.awardedSuppressed: award count withheld with the rate
fw.cellNote: Award counts appear only beside the completion rate; cells under {n} are suppressed.
fw.mineBody: As fellow, supervisor or host university (HR and auditors see every fellowship).
fw.mineNone: You are not part of any fellowship
fw.footer: Sample fellowships with synthetic fellows; host projects are screened research challenges or ADVANCE studies (planning assumption, no deployment decision implied).
fw.notFoundBody: It does not exist or you are not part of it.
fw.advanceBody: The host is an ADVANCE technology study: a planning assumption, no deployment decision implied.

patternNote.nest_fellowship: NEST pattern: the fellow gains the skill and the network inside a real project.
patternNote.sponsored_study: MSCFP pattern: funding for study plus a placement, so study is paired with industry exposure.

ms.title: Milestones
ms.rule: The fellow submits (the university submits its own milestones); the named supervisor or HR signs off, never the person who submitted.

consequence.submit: The supervisor is notified to sign off this milestone.
consequence.sign_off: The milestone is signed off and recorded in the evidence ledger. When every required milestone is signed off, the fellowship is complete.
consequence.return: The milestone goes back to the fellow with your note.

problem.title: Give the title in English and Arabic (3 to 160 characters each).
problem.fellow: Enter the fellow (an applicant or a member of staff).
problem.university: Sponsored study needs the host university.
problem.host: Choose a published research challenge or an ADVANCE technology study.
problem.supervisor: The supervisor must be an active ENEC role card, not the fellow.
problem.dates: The planned span is 90 days to four years.
problem.placement: Describe the placement (sponsored study needs it; up to 300 characters).
problem.clean: ADVANCE text must not carry headcounts or site wording.
problem.duplicate: This fellow already has a fellowship starting that year.

wf.intro: Run the fellowship programme: completion first (from milestones, suppressed under 10), then breakdowns, overdue milestones, awards and withdrawals.
wf.noneVisible: No fellowship rows for your role
wf.noneVisibleBody: HR analysts see the aggregates above; the HR director sees every fellowship.
wf.withdrawConsequence: The fellowship is withdrawn and recorded in the evidence ledger. It stays in the completion rate as due and not completed.
wf.fellowHint: Synthetic person id, for example ap-160
wf.supervisorHint: A role-card person id, for example p-training-mgr
wf.awardConsequence: The fellowship is created with five milestones from its pattern and recorded in the evidence ledger.
